name: GHO
who_can_redeem: GHO is minted through governance-approved facilitators, including Aave protocol integrations. Borrowers repay GHO debt to release collateral, while supported GHO Stability Modules provide bounded conversion paths against approved assets.
redemption_region_notes: Access depends on supported Aave markets, facilitator capacity, bridge state, GSM inventory, interfaces, and current governance parameters.
redemption_notes: SOG separates debt repayment, GSM conversion, canonical bridging, and secondary-market liquidity. GHO is not represented as a direct claim on a bank account or issuer cash reserve.
summary: USD-pegged stablecoin governed by the Aave DAO and issued through governance-approved facilitators. GHO began on Ethereum with the Aave V3 Ethereum and FlashMinter facilitators and later expanded through canonical bridge and GSM infrastructure.
notes: Batch C promotion. The current complete facilitator-capacity and remote-deployment inventory remains a separately tracked source-review area.

name: BOLD
who_can_redeem: Any BOLD holder can redeem BOLD directly through Liquity V2 for a routed mixture of supported collateral at face value minus protocol fees, subject to branch state, oracle state, and system rules.
redemption_region_notes: Access depends on Ethereum, supported interfaces, branch availability, oracle operation, and current contract state. Cross-chain BOLD representations must be separated from Ethereum issuance.
redemption_notes: BOLD is distinct from LUSD. It is issued in Liquity V2 against WETH, wstETH, and rETH branches, with borrower-set interest rates and direct protocol redemption.
summary: Liquity V2's USD-pegged stablecoin, issued against WETH, wstETH, and rETH collateral. BOLD uses immutable issuance contracts, borrower-set interest rates, branch-specific Stability Pools, and direct routed redemptions.
notes: Batch C promotion. The May 2025 date represents the currently documented live deployment after earlier V2 deployment and redeployment work.

name: USD0
who_can_redeem: USD0 minting and redemption can occur through supported direct collateral-provider paths or indirect market and protocol routes, subject to eligible collateral, current interfaces, liquidity, governance, and compliance requirements.
redemption_region_notes: Direct issuance and redemption may depend on collateral-provider eligibility and jurisdiction. Secondary-market access does not establish a direct redemption right.
redemption_notes: SOG records USD0 separately from bUSD0, sUSD0, and USD0a. Yield, lock-up, leverage, and reward-bearing products are adjacent layers rather than the same canonical asset.
summary: USD-pegged stablecoin of the Usual ecosystem, backed by short-duration tokenized real-world assets such as sovereign debt instruments and designed for 1:1 minting and redemption through supported collateral pathways.
notes: Batch C promotion. Official materials place the launch and growth phase in 2024, but a single durable day-level launch date has not yet been fixed.

name: Resolv USD
who_can_redeem: Before the March 2026 incident, USR mint and redemption used protocol requests, collateral, and authorized off-chain completion services. After the incident, Resolv reported that most operations were paused and that eligible pre-incident USR holders were being compensated on a 1:1 basis.
redemption_region_notes: Access depends on the current recovery process, supported contracts, counterparties, jurisdictional terms, and protocol restart decisions.
redemption_notes: SOG separates USR from RLP, stUSR, and wstUSR. Yield exposure, insurance risk, and wrapped receipt tokens are not treated as the same canonical asset.
summary: Crypto-native USD-pegged stablecoin from Resolv, supported by a delta-neutral collateral strategy and a separate RLP risk-absorption layer. USR entered a restricted recovery state after an unauthorized 80 million USR minting incident on 22 March 2026.
notes: Batch C promotion. Exact original launch date and the final post-incident operating model remain open questions.
